findings.text: blocking: _recent_landed parses the edited stamp with datetime.fromisoformat at reckon/fleet_index.py:146 rather than the shared parser in reckon/_timestamps.py, so tests/test_structural_invariants.py::test_only_the_shared_parser_calls_fromisoformat now reports two offenders — ['crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:_review_dispatch_instant', 'fleet_index.py:_recent_landed'] at a92eb199 against ['crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:_review_dispatch_instant'] at 733b71f4c, both EXIT=1 — and the newly added name hides behind the pre-existing base failure, so the guard that exists to stop a second parser appearing silently is exactly the one this change defeats; the run's own next commit b50073358 ('fix(fleet): parse delivery stamps with shared helper') repairs it and lies outside the reviewed range, so whatever is promoted must include that commit or the reviewed head must not be promoted alone.

follow-on: the nav_key composition at reckon/fleet_index.py:152-155 re-spells a rule the repository already owns at reckon/reader_pdf.py:47-60 (reader_hash: 'f"{artifact_type}:{'archive:' if archived else ''}{slug}"') and at docs/ui/state-loader.js:98, inline rather than extending or wrapping either owner, so the archive-key grammar now lives in three places and can drift the moment one of them is edited.
